case_name: A one-minute explainer with a fixed sequence of facts: the citric acid cycle
title: Citric acid cycle, a 60 s explainer
tests: Tests a one-minute explainer with a fixed order of facts: whether the system keeps one consistent diagram across a minute, letters short labels correctly, narrates the steps in order, and stays within the length.

faults.what: Scientifically incorrect and changing labels: oxaloacetate is labelled 5C in the second frame, and isocitrate is labelled 5C in the final frame. Both errors undermine the carbon accounting central to this lesson.

The supplied narration stops after succinyl-CoA formation and ends with the garbled sentence 'Neither dispill carbon is newly arrived.' It does not explain ATP production, FADH2 production, or oxaloacetate regeneration.

Molecule labels become distorted or obscured, including the succinate dehydrogenase box, and the opening acetyl-CoA label is misspelled. Repeated citrate labels also make the opening diagram confusing.
Later framing crops important diagram content and the title; the final sample includes a partial duplicate mitochondrion at the right edge and a cut-off summary panel below.

judge.summary: The video has the requested mitochondrial loop format, but inaccurate labels, degraded diagrams, and incomplete narration make it unsuitable as a biology explainer without a redo.

must_haves.item: The cycle is shown as a loop, as a simple clean 2D animation inside a mitochondrion, not live action.
must_haves.why: The frames show a flat illustrated mitochondrion containing a circular arrow pathway, although the diagram loses clarity later.

must_haves.item: The steps appear in order: acetyl-CoA joins oxaloacetate to form citrate; two carbons leave as CO2; NADH, FADH2 and ATP are produced; oxaloacetate is regenerated.
must_haves.why: The opening reaction and two CO2 releases are supported, and energy-carrier labels appear later, but the full ordered sequence and oxaloacetate regeneration are not clearly demonstrated. Incorrect carbon counts further compromise the explanation.

must_haves.item: Calm English narration is audible and explains each step as it happens.
must_haves.why: English speech is reported, but the transcript covers only the early reactions and ends in a garbled sentence rather than explaining every step.

must_haves.item: The key molecules are labelled on screen as they appear, and the title 'Citric acid cycle' is shown.
must_haves.why: The title is clearly shown, but key labels are misspelled, scientifically incorrect, obscured, or cropped.
The reported duration is 62.1 seconds and the supplied frames are widescreen 16:9.
The speech transcript does not establish whether background music is absent.
